title: Where is the barrier?
caption: Reproductive barriers act in order. Prezygotic barriers stop fertilisation: the groups never meet or breed together, do not accept each other, or their gametes cannot fuse. Postzygotic barriers act after a zygote forms: the hybrid does not survive, is sterile, or its offspring are weak.
alt: A flow chart of questions from meeting and mating to hybrid fertility, each 'no' leading to a barrier: habitat or temporal, behavioural or mechanical, gametic, hybrid inviability, hybrid sterility or hybrid breakdown.
description: Do the groups meet in the same habitat and breed at the same time? If not: habitat or temporal isolation.
Do they accept each other as mates and fit together? If not: behavioural or mechanical isolation.
Can their sperm and eggs fuse? If not: gametic isolation.
Does the hybrid zygote develop and survive? If not: hybrid inviability.
Is the hybrid fertile? If not: hybrid sterility, as with mules.
Are later hybrid generations fertile and fit? If not: hybrid breakdown. If they are, there is no reproductive barrier.

q1.q: Do the groups meet in the same habitat and breed at the same time?

q2.q: Do they accept each other as mates, with structures that fit?

q3.q: Can their sperm and eggs fuse?

q4.q: Does the hybrid zygote develop and survive?

q6.q: Are later generations of hybrids fertile and fit?

none.outcome: No barrier: the groups are not reproductively isolated
